description: Return a `graph_hash` field on every `Extract` response so consumers can detect "graph unchanged since last call" without redoing their own diff. No internal cache in this scenario.

requirements.description: Every Extract response must include a graph_hash field containing a stable content-addressable hash (SHA-256 or equivalent) of the serialized graph content. The hash must be computed after normalization and serialization so that byte-identical graphs produce byte-identical hashes. Consumers can use graph_hash to detect unchanged graphs without performing their own diff. The scenario does not implement an internal cache; it recomputes the hash on each response.
requirements.title: Content-Hash Graph Fingerprint on Extract Response

validation.notes: Test that two Extract calls on the same unchanged module return identical graph_hash values
Test that an Extract call after adding a new file to the module returns a different graph_hash
Test that graph_hash is computed from the serialized graph content (not from file mtimes or other metadata)
Test graph_hash field is present and non-empty on all Extract responses including partial graph responses
Test hash algorithm is SHA-256 and output is hex-encoded string
Integration test: extract same fixture twice, assert graph_hash values are identical
Integration test: modify a fixture file, extract again, assert graph_hash changes
graph_hash field is present in the Connect-RPC response and accessible via CLI output and UI display
Hash computation adds <50ms overhead to any extraction (verified by benchmark)
Consumers can implement change-detection polling using graph_hash without additional infrastructure
graph_hash is documented in the proto field comment explaining its purpose and computation basis

title: Content-Hash Cache Hint
